test_title: PYST 22: SSC GD Constable 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 13 Feb, 2025 - Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: 400 apples were bought at ₹1210 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹860. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of apples.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost price per apple = 1210 ÷ 100 = ₹12.10

Profit per apple = 860 ÷ 400 = ₹2.15

Selling price per apple = 12.10 + 2.15 = ₹14.25

Selling price per dozen = 14.25 × 12 = ₹171

**∴ The correct answer is ₹171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total apples bought = 400

Cost Price (CP) per 100 apples = ₹1210

Total Profit = ₹860

1 Dozen = 12 apples

**Formula Used:**

Total SP = Total CP + Total Profit

SP per dozen = (Total SP ÷ Total apples) × 12

 
 Total CP = ₹4840
 
 
 Profit = ₹860
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total SP (400 apples) = ₹5700
 
 
 SP per Dozen = ₹171

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP of 400 apples = 1210 × (400 ÷ 100) = ₹4840

⇒ Total SP of 400 apples = 4840 + 860 = ₹5700

⇒ SP of 1 apple = 5700 ÷ 400 = ₹14.25

⇒ SP of 1 dozen (12 apples) = 14.25 × 12 = ₹171

**∴ The correct answer is ₹171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Profit & Loss Formulas

Profit = Selling Price (SP) − Cost Price (CP) | Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Unitary Method

To find the price of multiple items, calculate the price of a single item first (Total Value ÷ Total Quantity), then multiply by the required number of items.

Common Quantities

1 Dozen = 12 items | 1 Score = 20 items | 1 Gross = 144 items (12 dozens).
